guide.summary: Peter was transformed from a man who denied Jesus into a courageous leader of the Church. John was his faithful companion. Stephen was the first martyr, demonstrating that faith is worth more than life. These heroes teach us about courage, faithfulness and sacrifice.

keyVerses.text: But Peter and John answered: We must obey God rather than men.
The apostles left the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
And they stoned Stephen as he called out: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

exercises.prompt: What was Peter like before Pentecost?
exercises.text: Peter had a very distinctive characteristic before receiving the Holy Spirit.
exercises.explanation: Peter had denied Jesus three times out of fear, but then he was transformed.

exercises.statement: After Pentecost, Peter became a courageous and fearless man.
exercises.explanation: Peter's transformation is dramatic: from denier to bold preacher.

exercises.prompt: What was Peter's response when ordered not to preach?
exercises.text: The authorities tried to silence Peter, but he answered with courage.
options: We must obey God rather than men
I will obey and stop preaching
exercises.answer: We must obey God rather than men
exercises.explanation: Peter declared that his obedience to God is more important than obedience to men.

exercises.text: Peter's courageous response
tokens: Whether it is right in the sight of God
to listen to you more than to God
distractors: speaking about what we have seen

exercises.statement: Peter's courage came from his personal strength and determination.
exercises.explanation: Peter's courage came from the Holy Spirit, not from his own strength.

exercises.prompt: What was the relationship between Peter and John?
exercises.text: These two apostles worked together frequently in Acts.
options: They were inseparable companions in the work
exercises.answer: They were inseparable companions in the work
exercises.explanation: Peter and John worked together preaching, healing and facing persecution.

exercises.statement: John was an unschooled man, but had met with Jesus.
exercises.explanation: Luke observes that Peter and John were unschooled men, but the courage came from Jesus.

exercises.prompt: What surprised the leaders about Peter and John?
exercises.text: Even without formal education, they impressed with their message.
options: Their courage and confidence in Jesus
exercises.answer: Their courage and confidence in Jesus
exercises.explanation: It was clear that their authority came from a real encounter with Jesus.

exercises.statement: John's faithfulness to Peter is an example of Christian companionship.
exercises.explanation: John remained by Peter's side in preaching, healing and even imprisonment.

exercises.text: A man full of faith and the Holy Spirit in the early Church.
exercises.explanation: Stephen was chosen among the seven deacons to serve the widows.

exercises.statement: Stephen performed signs and wonders and faced verbal opposition.
exercises.explanation: Stephen not only served, but also performed miracles and testified.

exercises.text: His death was an extreme test of his faith in Jesus.
exercises.explanation: Stephen was the first Christian martyred, stoned for his faith.

exercises.text: Stephen's last prayer in Acts 7:59-60

exercises.statement: Stephen faced death with fear and regret of his faith.
exercises.explanation: Stephen faced death with peace, a vision of heaven and forgiveness for his killers.

exercises.prompt: What is the main lesson about persecution in Acts?
exercises.text: Peter, John and Stephen faced opposition in different ways.
options: Faith sustains us even in adversity
We must avoid persecution at any cost
Faith does not matter when there is opposition
We should use violence to defend ourselves
exercises.answer: Faith sustains us even in adversity
exercises.explanation: All three remained faithful, demonstrating that faith transcends persecution.

exercises.statement: God abandons His servants when they face severe persecution.
exercises.explanation: God was present and empowered His servants even during the most severe persecution.

exercises.prompt: What did Peter and John show when imprisoned?
exercises.text: Their reaction demonstrates what true faith means.
options: Rejoicing to suffer for faith in Christ
exercises.answer: Rejoicing to suffer for faith in Christ
exercises.explanation: They left prison rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer for Jesus.

exercises.statement: The courage of these heroes is an inspiring model for Christians of all ages.
exercises.explanation: Their lives continue to inspire Christians to remain faithful in any circumstance.

exercises.text: Peter's journey is one of the greatest transformations in the Bible.
options: From fear to courage through the Holy Spirit
exercises.answer: From fear to courage through the Holy Spirit
exercises.explanation: Pentecost marked Peter's dramatic transformation.

exercises.statement: Peter and John faced imprisonment but continued preaching.
exercises.explanation: No threat silenced these heroes of the primitive faith.

exercises.text: Although he died young, his impact was great.
options: Witness of faith unto martyrdom and influence on young Saul
exercises.answer: Witness of faith unto martyrdom and influence on young Saul
exercises.explanation: Saul witnessed Stephen's death and later became Paul, the great apostle.

exercises.statement: The examples of Peter, John and Stephen show that true faith perseveres.
exercises.explanation: These three men demonstrated that Christian faith is enduring and transformative.
